guide.headline: Commanders want to run it down the Colts' throat
guide.hook: Washington's ground game has a real shot against a Colts run defense that ranks near the bottom of the league, while two standout players fight it out on the other side of the ball.

items.title: Commanders lean on the run
items.what: The Commanders rank No. 18 of 32 in rush success rate at 40 percent, nothing special on its own. But the Colts rank No. 30 against the run at 47 percent, a 39 percentile point gap that favors Washington staying on schedule. If the Commanders are rushing more than 20 times by halftime, their plan is working and third downs stay short.
items.when: First drive and every early-down snap for Washington.
items.who: Commanders run game vs Colts run defense

items.title: Warren is the Colts' breakout weapon
items.what: Tyler Warren is seeing 92 percent of offensive snaps and a 23 percent target share, with 18 catches for 89 yards and two touchdowns already this year. His production per game is up 301 percent from last season, and at 6-6, 256 pounds he's a problem in the seam for a Washington defense trying to contain him on third down.
items.when: Third down and anytime Warren releases up the seam.

items.title: Buckner hunts the quarterback
items.what: DeForest Buckner already has three sacks, two TFL and four QB hits this season, numbers that put him in the top one percent of NFL defensive linemen. He's playing 81 percent of defensive snaps as the Colts' No. 1 right defensive tackle, so he's on the field for nearly every passing down. Watch whether he has a second move when his first rush gets stonewalled.
items.when: Passing downs, especially third-and-medium or longer.

guide.cardLine: Washington's run game has a real edge on a Colts defense ranked No. 30 against the rush, while Tyler Warren and DeForest Buckner duel on the other side of the ball.
